```{python}
import json
from html import escape

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import Markdown, display
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

# Bundle the table script into the page instead of loading it from a CDN.
init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

cpu, cpu_meta = site.load("tech-value", "residuals")
gpu, gpu_meta = site.load("tech-value", "gpu_residuals")
DATA = {"cpu": cpu, "gpu": gpu}
META = {"cpu": cpu_meta, "gpu": gpu_meta}
NOUN = {"cpu": "CPUs", "gpu": "GPUs"}

# The pipeline's consensus verdicts, grouped into the four classes this page shows.
CLASS_OF = {
    "True architectural standout": "standout",
    "Small-core linearity artifact": "sensitive",
    "Linearity / regime artifact": "sensitive",
    "Entry-shader linearity artifact": "sensitive",
    "Memory / scaling bottleneck": "bottleneck",
}
CLASSES = {
    "standout": ("Standout candidate", "Higher than expected across models.", "#18b47b"),
    "sensitive": ("Model-sensitive", "Larger change between models.", "#f0b23e"),
    "near": ("Near expected", "Close to model predictions.", "#c4cad1"),
    "bottleneck": ("Scaling bottleneck", "Lower than expected, suggests scaling or configuration limits.", "#d9707a"),
}
FONT = dict(family="Inter, Segoe UI, system-ui, sans-serif", color="#8391a1", size=12)
AXIS = dict(showgrid=False, showline=True, linecolor="#8391a1", ticks="outside", zeroline=False)

for kind, df in DATA.items():
    if not df.empty:
        df["cls"] = df["consensus_verdict"].map(CLASS_OF).fillna("near")


def coverage_limited(r) -> bool:
    """Few disclosures, or every one from a single OEM: one configuration can carry the result."""
    return int(r["n_oems"]) <= 1 or int(r["n_results"]) < 4


def count(kind, cls):
    df = DATA[kind]
    return int((df["cls"] == cls).sum()) if not df.empty else 0


ICON = {
    "chev": '<path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/>',
    "warn": '<path d="M12 3l10 18H2z"/><path d="M12 10v5M12 18v.5"/>',
}


def icon(name, cls=""):
    return f'<svg class="op-ico {cls}" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">{ICON[name]}</svg>'
```

```{python}
def pct_ticks(lim):
    step = 20 if lim <= 100 else 40
    vals = list(range(-int(lim // step) * step, int(lim // step) * step + 1, step))
    return vals, [f"{v:+d}%" if v else "0%" for v in vals]


def scatter(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    lim = max(80, float(np.ceil(df[["residual_pct", "gbdt_residual_pct"]].abs().max().max() / 10) * 10))
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_shape(type="rect", x0=0, y0=0, x1=lim, y1=lim, fillcolor="rgba(24,180,123,0.09)", line_width=0, layer="below")
    fig.add_hline(y=0, line=dict(color="#55606c", width=1.2))
    fig.add_vline(x=0, line=dict(color="#55606c", width=1.2))
    hover = ("<b>%{customdata[0]}</b><br>%{customdata[1]}<br>OLS %{x:+.1f}% · Structural %{customdata[2]:+.1f}%"
             " · Nonlinear %{y:+.1f}%<br>%{customdata[3]} disclosures · %{customdata[4]} OEM(s)<extra></extra>")
    for cls in ("near", "sensitive", "bottleneck", "standout"):
        part = df[df["cls"] == cls]
        if part.empty:
            continue
        name, _, color = CLASSES[cls]
        custom = np.stack([part["processor"], [name] * len(part), part["structural_residual_pct"],
                           part["n_results"], part["n_oems"]], axis=-1)
        fig.add_scatter(
            x=part["residual_pct"], y=part["gbdt_residual_pct"], mode="markers", name=f"cls:{cls}",
            marker=dict(size=6 if cls == "near" else 8, color=color, opacity=0.75 if cls == "near" else 0.95,
                        line=dict(width=0.6, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)")),
            customdata=custom, hovertemplate=hover, showlegend=False,
        )
    fig.add_scatter(x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers", name="selected", hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=17, color="rgba(24,180,123,0.2)", line=dict(width=2.4, color="#0f8f6c")))
    vals, text = pct_ticks(lim)
    fig.update_layout(
        height=430, font=FONT, margin=dict(t=10, r=10, b=50, l=70),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[-lim, lim], tickvals=vals, ticktext=text, title="Score above / below OLS prediction (%)"),
        yaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[-lim, lim], tickvals=vals, ticktext=text, title="Score above / below nonlinear prediction (%)"),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color="#14233a"), dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


def raw(html):
    """Emit HTML as a raw block so pandoc does not re-parse it as markdown."""
    print(f"\n```{{=html}}\n{html}\n```\n")


def legend(kind):
    items = "".join(
        f'<li><span class="op-dot" style="background:{c}"></span><span><b>{n}</b><small>{d}</small></span></li>'
        for n, d, c in CLASSES.values()
    )
    raw(f'<aside class="op-legend"><ul>{items}</ul><hr><small>Classification also uses the structural model.</small>'
          '<div class="op-callout">Positive residual = measured score above model prediction.</div></aside>')


def pick(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    rows = [dict(name=r.processor, ols=round(r.residual_pct, 1), st=round(r.structural_residual_pct, 1),
                 nl=round(r.gbdt_residual_pct, 1), n=int(r.n_results), oems=int(r.n_oems),
                 cls=CLASSES[r.cls][0], limited=coverage_limited(r._asdict()))
            for r in df.itertuples()]
    standouts = df[df["cls"] == "standout"]
    default = (standouts if len(standouts) else df).sort_values("gbdt_residual_pct").iloc[-1]["processor"]
    opts = "".join(f'<option{" selected" if d["name"] == default else ""}>{escape(d["name"])}</option>'
                   for d in sorted(rows, key=lambda d: d["name"]))
    print(f"""```{{=html}}
<div class="op-pick" data-chips="{escape(json.dumps(rows), quote=True)}">
<div class="op-pick-name" data-f="name"></div>
<div class="op-pick-vals">
<div><span>OLS</span><strong data-f="ols"></strong></div>
<div><span>Structural</span><strong data-f="st"></strong></div>
<div><span>Nonlinear</span><strong data-f="nl"></strong></div>
<div class="op-cov"><b data-f="cov"></b><span class="op-cls" data-f="cls"></span><span class="op-warn" data-f="warn">{icon("warn")} Limited configuration coverage</span></div>
</div>
<label>Inspect a chip<select aria-label="Inspect a chip">{opts}</select></label>
</div>
```""")


def head(title, *ledes):
    raw(f"<h2>{title}</h2>" + "".join(f'<p class="op-lede">{t}</p>' for t in ledes))
```

```{python}
SHORT_GROUP = {
    "Intel oneAPI (LLVM)": "Intel oneAPI",
    "Oracle / Vendor Studio": "Oracle Studio",
    "SPECviewperf 15 (DX12 / Vulkan / OpenGL)": "SPECviewperf 15",
    "SPECviewperf 2020 (OpenGL / DX12)": "SPECviewperf 2020",
    "SPECviewperf 12.1 / 13 (Legacy OpenGL)": "SPECviewperf 12.1 / 13",
    "SPECworkstation (Full System + GPU)": "SPECworkstation",
    "SPECapc (Maya / Solidworks / Creo / 3ds Max)": "SPECapc",
}


def group_table(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    g = df.groupby("compiler_family").agg(
        chips=("processor", "size"), disclosures=("n_results", "sum"),
        spread=("tuning_spread_pct", "median"), ols=("residual_pct", "median"),
        nonlinear=("gbdt_residual_pct", "median"),
    ).reset_index()
    return g.sort_values("disclosures", ascending=False)


def spread_chart(kind):
    g = group_table(kind)
    g = g[g["chips"] >= 1].sort_values("disclosures")
    labels = [f"{SHORT_GROUP.get(f, f)} <span style='font-size:10px'>({c})</span>" for f, c in zip(g["compiler_family"], g["chips"])]
    fig = go.Figure()
    for y, v in zip(labels, g["spread"]):
        fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=0, x1=v, y0=y, y1=y, line=dict(color="#8391a1", width=1.5))
    fig.add_scatter(
        x=g["spread"], y=labels, mode="markers+text", text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in g["spread"]],
        textposition="middle right", textfont=dict(color="#8391a1", size=12),
        marker=dict(size=13, color="#18b47b", line=dict(width=1, color="white")),
        customdata=np.stack([g["chips"], g["disclosures"]], axis=-1),
        hovertemplate="%{y}<br>Median spread %{x:.1f} pts<br>%{customdata[0]} chips · %{customdata[1]} disclosures<extra></extra>",
        showlegend=False,
    )
    hi = float(np.ceil((g["spread"].max() * 1.25) / 5) * 5)
    fig.update_layout(
        height=max(240, 60 + 46 * len(g)), font=FONT, margin=dict(t=6, r=12, b=50, l=10),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, range=[0, hi], ticksuffix="%", title="Median same-chip residual spread (percentage points)"),
        yaxis=dict(showgrid=False, showline=False, ticks="", automargin=True),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color="#14233a"), dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


TIERS = {
    "cpu": ("l3_mb_per_core", [1.5, 3.0], ["Low L3", "Standard L3", "High L3"]),
    "gpu": ("bandwidth_gbps", [200, 500], ["Low bandwidth", "Standard bandwidth", "High bandwidth"]),
}
TIER_COLORS = ["#d9707a", "#f0b23e", "#18b47b"]
SYMBOLS = {"Intel": "circle", "AMD": "diamond", "NVIDIA": "circle", "Other": "square"}


def scaling_chart(kind):
    df = DATA[kind].dropna(subset=["cores_per_chip", "score_per_core"]).copy()
    col, cuts, names = TIERS[kind]
    df["tier"] = np.digitize(df[col].fillna(df[col].median()), cuts)
    fig = go.Figure()
    unit = "MB L3 / core" if kind == "cpu" else "GB/s"
    for t, name in enumerate(names):
        for vendor, symbol in SYMBOLS.items():
            part = df[(df["tier"] == t) & (df["vendor"] == vendor)]
            if part.empty:
                continue
            fig.add_scatter(
                x=part["cores_per_chip"], y=part["score_per_core"], mode="markers", showlegend=False,
                marker=dict(size=7, symbol=symbol, color=TIER_COLORS[t], opacity=0.85, line=dict(width=0.6, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)")),
                customdata=np.stack([part["processor"], part[col], part["residual_pct"]], axis=-1),
                hovertemplate=f"<b>%{{customdata[0]}}</b><br>%{{x:,.0f}} {'cores' if kind == 'cpu' else 'shaders'} · "
                              f"%{{y:.1f}} per {'core' if kind == 'cpu' else '1,000 shaders'}<br>%{{customdata[1]:.1f}} {unit} · "
                              "OLS %{customdata[2]:+.1f}%<extra></extra>",
            )
    lo, hi = df["cores_per_chip"].min(), df["cores_per_chip"].max()
    xt = [2 ** e for e in range(0, 16) if lo / 1.5 <= 2 ** e <= hi * 1.5]
    if kind == "gpu":
        xt = [v for v in (500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000) if lo / 1.5 <= v <= hi * 1.5]
    ylo, yhi = df["score_per_core"].min(), df["score_per_core"].max()
    yt = [m * 10 ** e for e in range(-1, 4) for m in (1, 2, 5) if ylo / 1.3 <= m * 10 ** e <= yhi * 1.3]
    fig.update_layout(
        height=330, font=FONT, margin=dict(t=6, r=10, b=50, l=64),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", tickvals=xt, ticktext=[f"{v:,}" for v in xt],
                   title="Cores per chip (log scale)" if kind == "cpu" else "Shaders per GPU (log scale)"),
        yaxis=dict(**AXIS, type="log", tickvals=yt, ticktext=[f"{v:g}" for v in yt],
                   title="Base score per core" if kind == "cpu" else "Score per 1,000 shaders"),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color="#14233a"), dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


def scaling_keys(kind):
    _, cuts, names = TIERS[kind]
    unit = "MB/core" if kind == "cpu" else "GB/s"
    bounds = [f"&lt; {cuts[0]:g} {unit}", f"{cuts[0]:g}–{cuts[1]:g}", f"&gt; {cuts[1]:g}"]
    tiers = "".join(f'<span title="{b}"><span class="op-dot" style="background:{c};margin:0"></span>{n}</span>'
                    for n, b, c in zip(names, bounds, TIER_COLORS))
    vendors = ["Intel", "AMD", "Other"] if kind == "cpu" else ["NVIDIA", "AMD"]
    shapes = "".join(f'<span><span class="op-shape {SYMBOLS[v]}"></span>{v}</span>' for v in vendors)
    raw(f'<div class="op-keys">{tiers}{shapes}</div>')
```

LABELS = {
    "processor": "Chip", "class": "Classification", "residual_pct": "OLS %",
    "structural_residual_pct": "Structural %", "gbdt_residual_pct": "Nonlinear %",
    "tuning_spread_pct": "Same-chip spread (pts)", "n_results": "Disclosures", "n_oems": "OEMs",
    "cores_per_chip": "Cores/chip", "l3_mb_per_core": "L3 MB/core", "score_per_core": "Score/core",
    "median_score": "Median score", "first_avail": "First available", "compiler_family": "Compiler",
    "config_memory": "Memory tested", "config_system": "System", "Disclosure": "Disclosure",
    "vram_gb": "VRAM GB", "bandwidth_gbps": "Bandwidth GB/s",
}


def ranking(kind):
    df = DATA[kind]
    table = df.assign(
        **{"class": df["cls"].map(lambda c: CLASSES[c][0]),
           "Disclosure": [f'<a href="{u}">report</a>' if u else "" for u in df["disclosure_url"]]}
    )
    cols = ["processor", "class", "residual_pct", "structural_residual_pct", "gbdt_residual_pct",
            "tuning_spread_pct", "n_results", "n_oems", "cores_per_chip"]
    cols += (["l3_mb_per_core", "score_per_core", "compiler_family", "config_memory"] if kind == "cpu"
             else ["vram_gb", "bandwidth_gbps", "compiler_family", "config_system"])
    cols += ["first_avail", "Disclosure"]
    table = table[cols].rename(columns=LABELS).rename(columns={"Cores/chip": "Cores/chip" if kind == "cpu" else "Shaders",
                                                              "Compiler": "Compiler" if kind == "cpu" else "Suite"})
    show(table.round(1), paging=True, pageLength=25, order=[[2, "desc"]], showIndex=False,
         classes="display compact", allow_html=True)


def breakdown(kind):
    g = group_table(kind).rename(columns={
        "compiler_family": "Compiler" if kind == "cpu" else "Suite", "chips": NOUN[kind],
        "disclosures": "Disclosures", "spread": "Median same-chip spread (pts)",
        "ols": "Median OLS %", "nonlinear": "Median nonlinear %",
    })
    show(g.round(1), paging=False, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")


def summary(title, note):
    print(f"<summary><b>{title}</b><span>{note}</span>{icon('chev', 'op-chev')}</summary>")

### GPUs by benchmark suite

A chip's **same-chip spread** is the gap, in percentage points, between its best and worst
result after the model's prediction is taken out. Each chip is placed in the group of its typical
submission (the result closest to its median), so a group's median says how much platform and
software move scores for chips that usually ship that way. The groups differ in which chips they
hold, so they are not a ranking of compilers or suites.
:::
</details>

<details class="op-detail">
```{python}
#| output: asis
summary("Models, definitions &amp; limitations", "OLS · Structural L1 · Nonlinear GBDT")
```
::: {.op-detail-body}

**Leave one chip out.** Every chip is scored by three models refitted without any result for
that chip, so a chip never helps predict itself. A chip's residual is the median over its
results of how far the measured score sits above (positive) or below (negative) the prediction.
CPUs need at least `{python} cpu_meta.get("min_results", 3)` published results to be ranked,
GPUs at least `{python} gpu_meta.get("min_results", 2)`.

**The three models.**

* **OLS** is a plain regression in logs on cores, clock, chips, SMT, L2 and L3 cache per core,
  vintage and vendor (for GPUs: shaders, boost clock, VRAM, memory bandwidth, mobile form factor
  and vendor).
* **Structural L1** is a robust (Huber or median) regression that adds diminishing returns on
  core or shader count and cache-by-density and bandwidth interactions.
* **Nonlinear GBDT** is a gradient-boosted tree model with median loss over the same
  specifications.

**Classes.** A *standout candidate* is above all three predictions (CPUs: OLS +10% or more,
structural and nonlinear +8% or more, and the OLS and nonlinear results within 25 points).
A *scaling bottleneck* is below all three (CPUs: −10%, −8%, −8%). A *model-sensitive* result
looks high on the straight-line OLS but much smaller once nonlinear scaling is allowed for
(CPUs: OLS +12% or more with the nonlinear result under +8% or 18 points lower); most are
small-core chips. GPU thresholds are similar and use the structural model to catch entry-level
cards. Everything else is *near expected*.

**Disclosure coverage.** A chip with fewer than four results, or with every result from one OEM,
is marked *limited configuration coverage*: one system or compiler choice can carry its
residual.

```{python}
#| output: asis
v = cpu_meta.get("verdict") or {}
if v:
    print(f"**Does the CPU model carry signal at all?** {v['statement']} See "
          "[Model and leaderboard](model.qmd).\n")
```

**Limitations.** A residual flags unexplained performance; it is not a quality score.
Architecture, memory configuration, compiler, BIOS settings and model fit all contribute, and
vendors choose which configurations to submit. The spread and scaling charts describe the
submitted results and do not separate these causes. GPU results span several SPEC GWPG suites and
resolutions, which are put on one scale before the models are fitted.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const signed = v => `${v > 0 ? "+" : v < 0 ? "−" : ""}${Math.abs(v).toFixed(1)}%`;
  const graphOf = cat => cat.querySelector(".op-plot .js-plotly-plot");
  document.querySelectorAll(".op-cat").forEach(cat => {
    const pick = cat.querySelector(".op-pick");
    if (!pick) return;
    const chips = JSON.parse(pick.dataset.chips);
    const select = pick.querySelector("select");
    const field = f => pick.querySelector(`[data-f="${f}"]`);
    const update = () => {
      const c = chips.find(d => d.name === select.value) || chips[0];
      field("name").textContent = c.name;
      for (const k of ["ols", "st", "nl"]) {
        field(k).textContent = signed(c[k]);
        field(k).classList.toggle("op-neg", c[k] < 0);
      }
      field("cov").textContent = `${c.n} disclosure${c.n === 1 ? "" : "s"} · ${c.oems} OEM${c.oems === 1 ? "" : "s"}`;
      field("cls").textContent = c.cls;
      field("warn").style.display = c.limited ? "block" : "none";
      const g = graphOf(cat);
      if (!g || !window.Plotly) return;
      const idx = g.data.findIndex(t => t.name === "selected");
      if (idx >= 0) Plotly.restyle(g, { x: [[c.ols]], y: [[c.nl]] }, [idx]);
    };
    select.addEventListener("change", update);
    cat._opUpdate = update;
    const g = graphOf(cat);
    if (g?.on) g.on("plotly_click", ev => {
      const name = ev.points?.[0]?.customdata?.[0];
      if (name && [...select.options].some(o => o.text === name)) { select.value = name; update(); }
    });
  });
  // Phone width: thin the tick labels and shorten axis titles so nothing is clipped.
  const SHORT = {
    "Score above / below OLS prediction (%)": "Above / below OLS (%)",
    "Score above / below nonlinear prediction (%)": "Above / below nonlinear (%)",
    "Median same-chip residual spread (percentage points)": "Median spread (pts)",
  };
  const fitPhone = g => {
    if (!g || !window.Plotly || g._opPhone || g.offsetWidth === 0 || g.offsetWidth >= 600) return;
    g._opPhone = true;
    const upd = { "margin.l": Math.min(g.layout.margin.l, 56) };
    for (const ax of ["xaxis", "yaxis"]) {
      const a = g.layout[ax], t = a.title?.text;
      if (SHORT[t]) upd[`${ax}.title.text`] = SHORT[t];
      if (a.tickvals && a.ticktext && a.tickvals.length > 7) {
        upd[`${ax}.tickvals`] = a.tickvals.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0);
        upd[`${ax}.ticktext`] = a.ticktext.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0);
      }
    }
    Plotly.relayout(g, upd);
  };
  const show = kind => {
    document.body.classList.toggle("op-gpu", kind === "gpu");
    document.querySelectorAll(".op-toggle button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b.dataset.tab === kind)));
    document.querySelectorAll(`.op-cat[data-kind="${kind}"]`).forEach(cat => {
      cat.querySelectorAll(".js-plotly-plot").forEach(g => { if (window.Plotly) { Plotly.Plots.resize(g); fitPhone(g); } });
      cat._opUpdate?.();
    });
  };
  document.querySelectorAll(".op-toggle button").forEach(b => b.addEventListener("click", () => {
    show(b.dataset.tab);
    try { history.replaceState(null, "", b.dataset.tab === "gpu" ? "#gpu" : location.pathname + location.search); } catch (e) {}
  }));
  show(location.hash === "#gpu" ? "gpu" : "cpu");
  const settle = () => show(document.body.classList.contains("op-gpu") ? "gpu" : "cpu");
  setTimeout(settle, 300);
  window.addEventListener("load", settle);
});
</script>
